answer.new_information: NVIDIA's own 2026-07-01 blog states it is introducing a new business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers under a revenue-sharing and credit-support model, with NVIDIA earning standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity, which it describes as a recurring usage-linked earnings stream. Supported by the text: the model is announced and its structure is described by the company. Not supported: any dollar size, number of contracts, share split, credit-support amount or terms, accounting treatment, start date, or whether any customer has signed. Sharon AI's CEO quote and the Firmus item (campus expected to scale to 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs, a plan not a delivery) are partner statements carried in NVIDIA's blog, with no independent confirmation in this record. Evidence needed to resolve: NVIDIA filings or call commentary quantifying revenue from this model and its receivables or guarantees to AI clouds; named signed agreements with terms; partner disclosures of capacity energised and GPUs installed; and the size of any credit support extended.
answer.new_question: Does NVIDIA's revenue-sharing and credit-support model with AI clouds add material recurring NVDA revenue, and what credit exposure does NVIDIA take on through the credit support?
answer.independent_judgement: Supported conclusion: NVIDIA has publicly announced a new model that pairs product sales to AI clouds with a revenue share on their cloud revenue and credit support, aimed at AI-native and enterprise customers. Hypothesis: this could broaden NVDA's demand base and add a usage-linked revenue line, while the credit support could shift financing risk onto NVIDIA's balance sheet. Missing bridge: no disclosed contract values, no share terms, no credit-support size or collection history, and no evidence that partner capacity (Sharon AI, Firmus) is financed or delivered on the stated timetable. The record is a company statement with no independent test, so it supports the existence and design of the model, not its economic size or sign.
